stateAfterThisRound: THE WIDE TITLES' SHEET GEOMETRY, FITTED TO THEIR OWN FILES, AND A SHARED LATER WALL. TH16, TH17 and TH18 each had a named parse failure; the missing number was where a title's group table begins, and each title's own sheet answers it when a candidate must walk every group to a terminator with interval>0 and finite angle/speed and the ladder climbs then repeats. TH14 is the control and the port's own constants are a fit. A first pass read the floats at +0x10/+0x14 where ShotSpec keeps them at +0x14/+0x18, which is a fit the engine rejected; reading the recorded offsets left TH18 unique and left the rows: TH16 table 0x190, base 0x1B8, stride 0x58, groups 10; TH17 table 0xE0, base 0x130, stride 0x58, groups 20; TH18 table 0xE0, base 0x1DC, stride 0x5C, groups 40, with the stride the one number that differs inside the wide family (TH18 walks 40/40 groups at 0x5C and 0/40 at 0x58, TH17 the other way). A successful parse now prints what it read on stdout, so the boot does not read as six console errors: th16 pl00.sht version=4 groups=10 specs=40 max_power=4 step=40, th17 pl00a.sht version=5 groups=20 specs=98, th18 pl00.sht version=5 groups=40 specs=59, which is the second instrument for the rows. All three then stop at the same, later wall: title compositor initialization failed - an ANM update script reaching opcode 3 with sprite 0xffff - which is the next measured piece. Keepers hold: title 13 PASS 694 state and 250 random-polar cases with 68 ANM resources and the stop/layer regression, geometry pass 3 fail 0, the browser record gate passes.

perTitleFindings.subject: five of the fixture's six game entries are accepted, only the template initialiser is not
perTitleFindings.evidence: in oracle mode, one process each: 0x45fc90 ok, 0x4600a0 ok, 0x44bf6a ok, 0x460fe0 ok, 0x4610d0 an ordinary guest fault, 0x402520 the wasm trap
perTitleFindings.port: the one blocker for a whole-corpus oracle run is 0x402520, the fixture's first game call

perTitleFindings.subject: the fixture's first game call runs again, past one relocated block
perTitleFindings.evidence: a jump over the refused block at 0x402551 is accepted by the engine; P (seed) and Q (execute the block in the heap) leave the template identical (sha 0a12ba04f0167bf7), P reproduced across processes; dialogue.test.mjs moved from the wasm trap at anm-oracle.mjs:20 to a guest read of 0x0 at pc=0x45fbff on its own next line
perTitleFindings.port: tests/cpp/engine-block-standin.mjs is the stand-in; the box stays the instrument for engine questions

perTitleFindings.subject: eight suites, no wasm trap left
perTitleFindings.evidence: th12-rng passes 2/2; dialogue, damage-area, anm-scripts, bullet-manager, hud, score-popups and screen-fade each fail with a guest payload (read 0x0, read 0x8, write 0x1, write 0x0 at pc 0, read 0x24) or in node-side code
perTitleFindings.port: the next item is the null read at 0x45fbff in the ANM loader, with the 66.7 globals/constants tables as the likely source of the missing fixture-side state

perTitleFindings.subject: the ANM load's null read is the D3D8 device, and the fixture now mounts it
perTitleFindings.evidence: the decomp names FUN_0045fbf0 as (**(code**)(*DAT_004ce8f0 + 0x5c))(...) and the raw bytes show the nine pushes before call [ecx+0x5c]; the new tools/th-writers.py finds the single absolute writer of 0x4ce8f0 (a teardown that stores ebx=0); the mount moves the load fault from pc=0x45fbff to pc=0x46024a and the sweep keeps every suite free of wasm traps
perTitleFindings.port: anm-oracle.mjs mounts the device beside its texture stubs; anm-load-fault.mjs is the one-call-per-process instrument for where a load stops

perTitleFindings.subject: the stub argument count and the stub key had to be measured
perTitleFindings.evidence: the call pushes nine argument dwords: CT_ARGC=8 leaves the loader at pc=0x0, CT_ARGC=9 returns cleanly to pc=0x46024a; registerImport keys by dll!name and overwrites the entry, so a fixture and a probe sharing a key share an argc
perTitleFindings.port: anm-load-device.mjs registers a distinct key; the lesson is in section 71.4

perTitleFindings.subject: the ANM load completes: the record write-back, measured slot and all
perTitleFindings.evidence: CT_WRITE=0x20 (the eighth argument, the esi push) clears the null read at pc=0x46024a and reaches 0x460259; 0x24 and unset do not; the fixture stub now stores its texture interface into the record read from that argument
perTitleFindings.port: anm-oracle.mjs; detail in section 72.1-72.2

perTitleFindings.subject: all 47 shipped animation files load through the original loader
perTitleFindings.evidence: anm-load-all.mjs: assets=47 requested=47 tally={'ok': 47}; anm-load-fault.mjs returns ok for text.anm, front.anm and pl00.anm
perTitleFindings.port: the ANM stage of the fixture suite is whole; anm-load-all.mjs is its regression

perTitleFindings.subject: the eight suites are past the loader and fail in game code
perTitleFindings.evidence: dialogue pc=0x41cfe0, hud pc=0x41a6d0, enemy-animations pc=0x412e30, title-selection pc=0x407700, others node-side; no wasm trap; th12-rng 2/2
perTitleFindings.port: the next subjects are those addresses, with the shape of sections 70-72

perTitleFindings.subject: a fixture suite can call an address the table never measured
perTitleFindings.evidence: touch(0x412e30) returned it unchanged, so the native call executed th12 mid-instruction (read of 0 at pc=0x412e30, no prologue byte); the twin search gives an ambiguous prologue and a unique body match (run 21) at 0x004154d0, corroborated by sub esp 0x310 vs 0x308; routing the call through touch moves the fault to pc=0x415518 inside the matched function
perTitleFindings.port: docs/porting/oracle-th11-th12.json gains the measured row; fixture-address-audit.mjs lists this class for every fixture file

perTitleFindings.subject: the next translation is a structure field offset
perTitleFindings.evidence: th12 0x415512 `mov esi,[ebx+0x174c]` against th11 `mov esi,[ebx+0x1614]`, with the following four instructions byte-identical and the null read at 0x415518 decaying to address 4
perTitleFindings.port: a field-offset table per structure, in the shape of the address tables

perTitleFindings.subject: a moved structure field is a measured row, like a moved function
perTitleFindings.evidence: tools/th-twin-fields.py (self-checked, 0 moved on an identical round trip) aligns 164 instructions of the executor pair with 1.000 operand-shape agreement and finds [ebx+0x1614] -> [ebx+0x174c] and [ebx+0x1580] -> [ebx+0x16b8] at the same +0x138, with the frame displacements each moving by the frame delta
perTitleFindings.port: docs/porting/oracle-fields-th11-th12.json + touchField() in fixture-addresses.mjs; enemy-animations.test.mjs moved from a guest fault at its first native call to a wasm-side trap on call 14 with none

perTitleFindings.subject: the oracle's own per-call budget and import census are worth carrying
perTitleFindings.evidence: the trap payload now names calls:14, entry:0x4154d0 and the six busiest imports; that one call runs GetProcAddress 97 times while the enter/leave pair is balanced and every import is registered once with the argument count it really has, so a long run is not what failed
perTitleFindings.port: machine.mjs counts calls, reports the entry and the census in the fault, and collects teardown traps into machine.teardown

perTitleFindings.subject: a code row must name an instruction boundary
perTitleFindings.evidence: m.replace() writes a five-byte jump at touch(0x4569c0); the row named 0x004621c1, one byte past the push ebp, so the guest executed that push, the jump stranded it, and the stub ret popped it: traced [esp] == ebp == 0x7effc48 with zero bytes at the trap EIP; th-twin-fields.py from the entries gives 23/24 aligned and shape 1.000, and the after-trace shows [esp] = 0x41c6d4, the return of `call 0x4621c0`
perTitleFindings.port: oracle-th11-th12.json row 0x4569c0 -> 0x004621c0 anchored with evidence; the row checker (target is an instruction boundary; suite-named addresses no row claims) is the next instrument

perTitleFindings.subject: an instrument that reads the stack can become the failure
perTitleFindings.evidence: readWords(EBP,2) with EBP=0 threw Guest memory bounds 0x0 + 8 from inside a hook on native call 2, which moved the suite failure and left recent empty; guarded, the trace reports the real call 14
perTitleFindings.port: machine.mjs trace is defensive; the lesson is recorded in section 75.1

perTitleFindings.subject: four code rows are not twins at all, and the window that matched was noise
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x455a00/0x455df0/0x455bc0/0x456020 -> 0x0044bf6a each report ENTRIES DO NOT ALIGN (src#3 <-> tgt#3); the distinctive body 8b4c24088b54240c occurs 4 times in th11 and 0 times in th12, while the prologue the candidate matched occurs 129 times in th12
perTitleFindings.port: the four rows are withdrawn with the evidence; anm-oracle spawn() must bind those create thunks host-side (th12 has no twin), as its own line 39 does for the allocation

perTitleFindings.subject: replace() does not translate, and 38 of 267 fixture sites depend on that
perTitleFindings.evidence: machine.mjs:63 writes the jump at the address it is given; tests/cpp/replace-site-audit.mjs finds 267 untranslated m.replace literals, 38 naming an address the table maps elsewhere, e.g. anm-resource.test.mjs:8 binds 0x46a720 while the table says memset is 0x477420 - and the suites that consume the withdrawn rows fail with UC_ERR_FETCH_UNMAPPED (code 6)
perTitleFindings.port: translate those literals (or keep target-namespace names deliberately); the audit tool lists them; a never-fired substitution is now visible through stubCensus in the verification artifact

perTitleFindings.subject: the guest was calling null API pointers: GetProcAddress returned 0
perTitleFindings.evidence: three suites died at the same native call with the same stub census and "address":"0x0" in the payload, with kernel32.dll!GetProcAddress called 97 times; after binding the name-backed stub with the table signature, all four passed the CRT (apiMisses 0); with argc 0 instead of 1 the same suites fell back to call 2 with "GetProcAddress -> EncodePointer, then address 0x0"
perTitleFindings.port: GetProcAddress returns a stub per requested name, behaviour and argc from the kernel32 table; EncodePointer/DecodePointer are identity at argc 1; apiMisses is in every artifact and trap dump so the API surface accumulates as a list

perTitleFindings.subject: m.call literals are the half of the namespace class that was actually fatal
perTitleFindings.evidence: the 38 m.replace translations changed no suite failure code (hypothesis falsified); the 18 m.call sites did: anm-resource calls=7 -> 379 and now runs inside 0x45fc90, anm-interpreter now runs inside 0x402520
perTitleFindings.port: tests/cpp/replace-site-audit.mjs audits both kinds and reads 0/0; 56 sites in 30 files translated

perTitleFindings.subject: the fixture layer is th11-shaped in 487 places: counted, not estimated
perTitleFindings.evidence: th-twin-rows.py --calls over tests/cpp: 498 literals, 9 known target addresses, 0 known source addresses, 2 aligned, 487 unknown-namespace and not the same code in th12, several decoding mid-instruction
perTitleFindings.port: the census mode is the keeper; each of the 487 is a measurement waiting to be taken, and the ones with a consequence in a named suite come first

perTitleFindings.subject: rank then decide: the search is a rank, the pair is a measurement
perTitleFindings.evidence: three recurring addresses measured and anchored (0x452010 -> 0x0045cdf0 41/42, 0x44b4b0 -> 0x00455630 20/24, 0x44fd10 -> 0x0045a3c0 21/29); 0x451ef0 left out because its best candidate aliases 0x452010 target at only 16/42, and anm-renderer still stops at 0x451ef0
perTitleFindings.port: th-twin-rows.py --search --prefilter entries, then --pair; the 15 call sites were translated and both audits read 0

perTitleFindings.subject: a JavaScript throw inside a hook is still possible from the fixture side
perTitleFindings.evidence: laser-line fails with Guest memory bounds 0x0 + 48, which is machine.view() being called with address 0 from a fixture, not a guest fault
perTitleFindings.port: guard the fixture-side accesses the way machine.mjs guards its own; the guest's real failure must not be replaced by the instrument's

perTitleFindings.subject: the harness is th12-shaped and must not be translated; suites are th11-shaped
perTitleFindings.evidence: the batch mapped six helpers.mjs addresses (RTC init, ioinit, memcpy, ...) and nine of ten suites died at native call 3 with entry=0x48801d; then, with the table reverted and the rows present, anm-load-all still failed until tests/cpp was restored - the translator had wrapped helpers.mjs and world-oracle.mjs literals in touch(...)
perTitleFindings.port: translator --tests-only; replace-site-audit.mjs reports suites and support files separately (0 in suites, 4 replace + 2 call in support files on purpose); the harness bootstrap addresses are transcribed from th12 and stay raw

perTitleFindings.subject: one pass measured 87 of 249 queue addresses, including the wall named last round
perTitleFindings.evidence: th-twin-batch.py: wildcard-regex scan of .text then entry-alignment scoring; 87 at paired >= 0.90 (12-62 instructions, shape 1.000), 162 unresolved; 0x408f20 -> 0x40a250 makes bullet-manager report entry=0x40a250 and hud move from call 8 to call 22
perTitleFindings.port: the batch is a ranker: apply only paired 1.000 with >= 12 instructions and never a harness-named source; the six weaker measurements wait in tools/tmp/twin-batch-300.json

perTitleFindings.subject: the fault builder replaced the fault it was building (second occurrence)
perTitleFindings.evidence: laser-line failed with Guest memory bounds 0x0 + 48; the stack named machine.mjs:96 reading readWords(ESP,12) with ESP=0 while building the fault; after guarding every read the suite reports the guest fault: pc=0x42564a, esp=0x0 recorded as unavailable, pop ebp; ret 4
perTitleFindings.port: machine.mjs line 96/105 read through a bounds() helper that records which register was unavailable; the fault is always built and always names the guest state

perTitleFindings.subject: the wildcard scan needed a relaxation to measure short and pointer-heavy functions
perTitleFindings.evidence: --span 0x40 --min-run 5 measured 31 more addresses; 22 passed the strict rule (paired 1.000, >= 12 instructions) and were anchored, including 0x420d80 -> 0x423250, the config suite wall; 36 sites in 26 suite files translated; census 487 -> 289
perTitleFindings.port: the batch pass takes --span and --min-run; the strict application rule and the harness-namespace exclusion stay unchanged, and sub-threshold measurements are left in tools/tmp/twin-batch-301.json

perTitleFindings.subject: an address inside an anchored function is derived by instruction index, not searched
perTitleFindings.evidence: --derive maps the anchored pair once and reads off the same-index instruction, then verifies on the row's own window; 0x424ea0 -> 0x428520 (paired 1.000, 28 instructions) and 0x424ee0 -> 0x428560 both came out, and both laser suites moved from calls=17/esp=0x0 to calls=18
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-twin-batch.py --derive: bases are anchored/measured rows, the derivation is a row with its own evidence, and the entry rule is re-checked on the derived window

perTitleFindings.subject: a ranked tie between near-duplicate functions is settled by the caller, not the score
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x4250b0 and 0x4270f0 have identical ranked candidate lists (0x4287c0 / 0x42ab80, both 0.909, shape 1.000); assigned in address order, laser-line enters 0x4287c0 and laser-infinite enters 0x42ab80 - two different targets, where a crossed assignment would have sent both to one
perTitleFindings.port: the batch leaves an aliased target aside unless the two SOURCE windows are byte-identical; the tie is then resolved by the suite that calls each address and recorded as corroboration by use

perTitleFindings.subject: an offset/address unit mismatch made a correct algorithm return zero
perTitleFindings.evidence: the per-address derivation reported 0 enclosing entries for 127 addresses; entry_bytes() returns blob offsets and the queue holds absolute addresses; after converting once at the boundary all 127 found distinct entries, none of them already measured
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-twin-batch.py converts entry offsets to addresses at the boundary and says so in a comment; the 127 distinct containers are the queue's own structure

perTitleFindings.subject: the harness exclusion is a region, not an equality
perTitleFindings.evidence: the enclosing entry of 0x47562a is 0x475620 and of 0x47b07b is 0x47b070 - the same CRT functions a few bytes earlier - so exact-equality let three CRT addresses through as th11 sources; five rows were dropped under a 0x200 neighbourhood rule
perTitleFindings.port: any source within 0x200 of an address helpers.mjs names is the harness; the measured containers are filtered by region before any row is written

perTitleFindings.subject: laser-line now fails inside the right function on a fixture precondition
perTitleFindings.evidence: calls=18, entry=0x4287c0, pc=0x42883c, code=8b 89 88 04 00 00 = mov ecx,[ecx+0x488] with ECX=0; before the rows it was esp=0 and a return path unwinding past its frame
perTitleFindings.port: the fixture must build the laser manager object the initialiser reads; the namespace class for this suite is closed and the remaining class is state setup

perTitleFindings.subject: a function that is called is a function; a 16-aligned address is a guess
perTitleFindings.evidence: the alignment-based entry index offered 60076 entries per image and the container pass it drove measured 8 of 123 with first instructions like add byte ptr [eax],al and or bl,ch at one pair; the call-target index offers 27554 and the same pass produced containers that verify at 27-29 instructions, with derivations at 20-22
perTitleFindings.port: call_targets() - every direct call rel32 target plus padding entries - is used for the container of a queued address and for the fallback candidate list, with in-range filtering because a call target may be a thunk outside .text

perTitleFindings.subject: derivation through a container can be stronger evidence than a window measurement
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x403511 and 0x403528 were measured by the wildcard scan at 11 and 10 instructions and set aside in section 301; derived through their container they pair 20 instructions at paired 1.000
perTitleFindings.port: when a short window measurement and a derivation disagree in strength, the derivation wins and the weak measurement stays aside in tools/tmp/

perTitleFindings.subject: a fixture addresses the guest, so every fixture literal is a source-namespace literal
perTitleFindings.evidence: the laser fixture wrote m.u32(0x4a8e94, manager) and the guest read the th12 global 0x4b44f4, so the manager pointer was zero and the read of its field trapped at pc=0x42883c; 325 such sites were found across 90 suites once the memory APIs were censused rather than only m.call and m.replace
perTitleFindings.port: tools/tmp/translate-305.mjs rewrites the memory APIs' address arguments and the mapped field offsets; a suite literal is a th11 literal wherever it appears, while the harness stays th12-shaped by construction

perTitleFindings.subject: a field offset is not a key: the alias rule applies to records
perTitleFindings.evidence: the field table held 0x474 -> 0x1140 for the enemy record while the laser manager's [ecx+0x474] moves to +0x488, measured on the aligned pair 0x4250b0 <-> 0x4287c0 (31 moved displacements over 69 pairs, shape agreement 1.000)
perTitleFindings.port: field rows carry the record they were measured on; only ebx-relative displacements of the manager were taken, [esp+...] frames and a different object ([esi+0x404]) were excluded

perTitleFindings.subject: a translator that rewrites a file must leave it compilable
perTitleFindings.evidence: the import guard asked for `touch` while 89 inserted sites needed `touchField`, so four suites failed with ReferenceError: touchField is not defined instead of on their subject; after the repair enemy-frame fails at pc=0x454d25 and enemy-movement at pc=0x4615dd, i.e. on their own code
perTitleFindings.port: the guard asks for the identifier it is about to insert; tools/tmp/repair-imports-305.mjs is re-runnable and repaired four files

perTitleFindings.subject: a test that cannot find its input has not tested anything
perTitleFindings.evidence: the census found 31 of 142 suites (22%) failing before they ran, on three hard-coded paths: th11.dat x16 under a localized-copy directory absent from the checkout, reference/native/d3dx9_37.dll x14, one analysis artifact; none of them a port defect
perTitleFindings.port: tests/cpp/originals.mjs resolves reference assets from the environment, the runtime reference tree, the runtime parent (including the [...] convention), the game installs and the system directories, and throws with the whole search when it cannot

perTitleFindings.subject: the machine spells its installs with numbers while the titles use names
perTitleFindings.evidence: the first resolver found C:\Windows\SysWOW64\d3dx9_37.dll and reported th11.dat missing, because it searched H:/Games/th/th11 rather than H:/Games/th/11
perTitleFindings.port: both spellings (th11 and 11) are searched; a reference that resolves on one machine and not another is the failure the module exists to remove

perTitleFindings.subject: the system D3DX9_37 copy is byte-identical to the required reference
perTitleFindings.evidence: graphics-oracle.mjs asserts sha256 c2ccb84c672a9d8966e82a28005a4269886ee304972ac3590c0b8a9c1622a3d8 and the load no longer throws Unexpected reference math DLL; the family now executes the relocated code and traps inside the image at pc=0x1177a35
perTitleFindings.port: the hash check stays and decides; the path became a search

perTitleFindings.subject: the disassembly dialect is a contract because the oracle parses it
perTitleFindings.evidence: the first dump generator uppercased whole lines: MOV EBX,0X455140, CALL 0x456c10, MOV DWORD PTR [...]; none of the ten dumps matched the suite's three patterns and scene-schedule still reported ENOENT or matched nothing, then after the formatter was fixed 004526f0 carries 27 CALL 0x00456c10 registrations and the suite fails on its own priority-order assertion
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-asm-dump.py writes artifacts/cpp/analysis/jp/functions/<addr>.asm in that dialect, with address and raw bytes per line so a transcription is checkable against the image

perTitleFindings.subject: a reading of the ABI is not a measurement
perTitleFindings.evidence: the D3DX9 trap at pc=0x1177a35 is mov eax,[ebp+8] as the first instruction, so machine.call was changed to establish a frame (EBP = ESP_at_entry + 4); the census after the change was identical to before - 19 passing, 53 trapping, 32/121 - and the change was reverted rather than kept
perTitleFindings.port: an interpretation that alters every call in the process needs a measured effect; the zero-filled section tails were kept only because they make the mapping match the loader, and are recorded as NOT the explanation of the trap

perTitleFindings.subject: a missing input is not a port defect, and the search that found nothing is evidence
perTitleFindings.evidence: the whole th11.exe was searched for the cipher rows as four dwords, as the eight key bytes, and for the th95 and th12 variants: none found, while the shape of 0x4581c0 (an idiv by the block) matches the Runtime code that derives those parameters
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-archive-ciphers.py exports the TH95 rows by parsing ResourceCrypt.cpp, so the constants exist in one place; reference/archive-ciphers.json is ignored like the other derived artifacts and is rebuilt by that one command

perTitleFindings.subject: a refusal clause list is an instrument when the failure is downstream of all of them
perTitleFindings.evidence: archive_read returned -1 for entries ascii.anm, bullet.anm, enemy.anm and front.anm, and evaluating Archive::read's four clauses against their measured triples gave [false, false, false, false] every time, which moved the named cause to the LZSS decode at Archive.cpp:52 where the only refusal is written != e.size
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-archive-probe.mjs prints each entry's triple, the four refusals and the read result, so the next round starts at the codec with 0x4426c0 already driven by the suite as its oracle

perTitleFindings.subject: the algorithm was right, the argument was missing, and the failure surfaced ten levels away
perTitleFindings.evidence: the port decoder transcribed into Python reproduced the original decoder's 178000 bytes exactly from window 8192 threshold 3 head 1 and a zero window, while archive_read returned -1 for every entry; the binding is archive_open(p,b,size,version) and the suite passed three arguments, so version 0 reached archive_crypt_table and its default case chose the TH14 rows; version 0 gave agreed 0 / refused 6 and version 11 gave agreed 6 / refused 0 on the same six entries
perTitleFindings.port: the suite passes generation 11 for th11.dat, archive_crypt_table returns nullptr for an unknown generation, and Archive::open refuses, so a forgotten version argument is named at the call instead of a refused read later: archive.test.mjs now passes 1/0 over all 184 entries and writes reference/assets plus reference/archive-manifest.json

perTitleFindings.subject: a classic-LZSS initial window is not this format, and a mask error looks like a port defect
perTitleFindings.evidence: candidates compared with the original's output: preload F threshold 2 produced 163025 bytes differing at 0, threshold 3 produced 177983 differing at 0, and a 4096-entry ring produced 178000 differing at 6353 - the offset where a reference first reaches past 4096, which is where the transcription rather than the port was wrong
perTitleFindings.port: the ring is 8192 entries with a 13-bit offset as Lzss.cpp already had it; the refuted candidates are recorded so the next reader does not re-derive them

perTitleFindings.subject: a defect class made mechanical finds a disciplined call base, and that is a result
perTitleFindings.evidence: an audit of 719 registered bindings against every call in every suite returned six candidates, and all six measured as spreads of exactly the arity their signatures ask for (resources.push fills two handles for pause_create, resources[3] shows the fourth handle in title-selection, three values for shake_start, pos and target)
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-arity-audit.py stays as the instrument that would catch the next silent-zero call; it reports candidates rather than defects because only the binding can say whether zero is wrong

perTitleFindings.subject: a suite with several walls must have its cases separated before a fix can be claimed
perTitleFindings.evidence: pause-end failed in one run with Unicorn code 6, Guest memory bounds 0x0 + 1200 and a wasm memory access out of bounds; three suites share the signature Guest memory bounds 0x1074 + 4, where 0x1074 is below the guest window and the read comes from the harness rather than from guest execution, so a binding returned a pointer that was read at 0x1074
perTitleFindings.port: the 0x1074 cluster is the named next item together with the case separation of pause-end and pause-menu; scene-schedule registration order and the D3DX9 in-image trap remain named as well

perTitleFindings.subject: an unsettled row is not a measurement, and the flag saying so was there
perTitleFindings.evidence: oracle-globals-th11-th12.json has a row for th11 0x4c3808 with ready:false and two candidates agreeing at one site out of nineteen; the translator used targetAddress 0x00001074 anyway, three suites failed with Guest memory bounds 0x1074 + 4, and the candidate traced back to a twin site that disassembles as int3 padding, so the emulator decoded noise into an address field
perTitleFindings.port: fixture-addresses.mjs applies settled rows only and rejects targets below the guest window, keeping a TH_TOUCH_TRACE list of what it skipped; the row is withdrawn in place with its reason, all six measured suites moved from the harness bounds error to a guest trap, and the twin finder must now refuse a non-instruction-start twin site before the table is re-measured (25 of 35 rows are unsettled)

perTitleFindings.subject: a global in an uninitialised tail cannot be paired by data
perTitleFindings.evidence: th11 .data VA 0x4a2000 vsize 0x28e40 but only 0x6400 raw, so 0x4c3808 lies 0x1a808 past the file-backed bytes; the same shape holds in th12 (.data VA 0x4ad000 vsize 0x29460 raw 0x6a00), and a context search finds no bytes to compare
perTitleFindings.port: the counterpart of such a global can only come from reference sites whose twins are verified instruction starts, which is the guard the tool needs before the table is re-measured

perTitleFindings.subject: two structural guards settle a twin site and refuse a plausible one
perTitleFindings.evidence: the failed candidate for th11 0x4c3808 came from a twin site that is int3 padding and a window match at min_run 8; re-measuring with an instruction-alignment check from the function-entry index plus an address-masked shape comparison settles 8 rows with 2 or more agreeing sites (0x4a7948 at 22 of 22) and leaves 0x4c3808 unsettled at 0 of 19 because its site 0x0040bf01 points at 0x004055a1 whose shape is a different instruction form
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-twin-globals-table.py writes a row as ready only when two or more checked sites agree, and the globals table is now 18 ready of 35; identity remains the fixpoint for the seventeen candidates, which is the honest state rather than a translation

perTitleFindings.subject: a block shift is not a measurement here, and the tool said so
perTitleFindings.evidence: the settled neighbours of 0x4c3808 measure different shifts: 0x4c3268 -> 0x4ce8cc is +0xb664 over four checked sites while 0x4c3280 -> 0x4ce8e8 and 0x4c3810 -> 0x4cee78 are +0xb668 over two each; the source globals are 0x18 apart and the counterparts 0x1c apart, so the data is not a rigid copy
perTitleFindings.port: the derivation route derived zero rows and declined rather than guessing; the old noise value 0x4cee70 is what one of the two competing shifts would give, which is why plausibility is not evidence

perTitleFindings.subject: a trap site is a witness: it names the global and the touch miss names the row
perTitleFindings.evidence: thirteen suites shared pc=0x45fbff addr=0x0; the site is mov eax,[0x4ce8f0] then mov ecx,[eax]; TH_TOUCH_LOG showed the run missing touch(0x4c3288) immediately before the fault, and the suite writes a pointer through that address precisely so the dereference is legal
perTitleFindings.port: the row 0x4c3288 -> 0x004ce8f0 is settled on three independent supports (one checked site, the behavioural proof, the neighbour shift +0xb668); the identical null wall is gone from all thirteen and replaced by five different later walls, two of which are assertions

perTitleFindings.subject: a touch miss just before a trap is evidence, and it is cheaper than a window score
perTitleFindings.evidence: touch() keeps a fixture constant when no row claims an address, which is correct, but a miss in the same run as a global-dereference trap identifies the row that should have translated it; the miss log also named a CODE address, 0x4540f0, pointing the same signal at the code table
perTitleFindings.port: TH_TOUCH_LOG stays in fixture-addresses.mjs as a diagnostic; the remaining 16 candidate rows can be picked off by running the suite that traps and reading the last misses

perTitleFindings.subject: a table can be audited by its own arithmetic, and the outlier was a defective row
perTitleFindings.evidence: the shift histogram of the 19 settled globals rows showed +0xb660 seven times and +0xb668 seven times, with 0x4a8d88 -> 0x01035c8d claiming +0xb8cf05 and supported by one site with no evidence; 0x01035c8d is outside every section of the th12 image (0x401000..0x4d8600)
perTitleFindings.port: the row is withdrawn, fixture-addresses.mjs rejects any target outside the image sections from docs/porting/oracle-image-sections.json, and removing the row unblocked the block-shift derivation of five more rows (the table is now 23 ready of 35)

perTitleFindings.subject: the pc=0x0 cluster is a stub ABI question, not a table defect
perTitleFindings.evidence: the trap payload has pc 0x0, calls 0, and recent[{at import, key fixture!texture dimensions, ret 0x46025b, drift -168}], so the jump to zero happens after the import stub returns; the two touch misses in the run are not the proximate cause
perTitleFindings.port: the stub for a four-argument stdcall import must return with ret 16 and a usable value; the next round reads the stub rather than the address table, and the remaining misses 0x4540f0 (code) and 0x4a5714 (global) stay on the table work-list

perTitleFindings.subject: the stub ABI hypothesis and the dispatcher hypothesis, both refuted at the same boundary
perTitleFindings.evidence: the call site pushes exactly three arguments (lea ecx,[esp+0x18]; push ecx; mov ecx,[edx+0x44]; push 0; push eax; call ecx) so argc:3 is right, and with an instrumented dispatcher player-motion logged no handler failure before the fault, so neither the convention nor a swallowed exception explains the jump to zero
perTitleFindings.port: helpers.mjs now balances the stack on every import path and records failures in m.importFailures (TH_IMPORT_STRICT re-raises); the pc=0x0 cluster is about a guest pointer that is never handed over, in a chunk loop that calls a vtable slot at [edx+0x44]

perTitleFindings.subject: a sweep needs an instruction boundary, and an entry index contains padding
perTitleFindings.evidence: the greatest entry below 0x46025b is 0x46022b and its sweep decodes as mov dh,bh; the first argument count was therefore two instead of three because the backward walk stopped at a mov between arguments, and th12 0x46022b is only a boundary in a sweep that is itself garbage
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-abi-count.py and tools/th-instruction-window.py keep only an entry in whose sweep the target address is exactly an instruction boundary, which is the same guard section 91 applied to twin sites and section 92 to code addresses

perTitleFindings.subject: the pc=0x0 cluster is a stack imbalance: a jump-table label called as a function
perTitleFindings.evidence: the executed-address ring ends at 0x44ae9d ret after pop edi; pop esi; pop ebx, and the call target 0x44acd0 is a case label of the function at 0x44aca0 whose prologue pushes those three registers and loads esi from 0x4b4534
perTitleFindings.port: a call into a function interior must supply the stack slots the epilogue pops, the x87 entry state (fld1 here) and the callee-saved values; 54 of the 116 literal interior call sites in the suites pop more than they push, across 36 files

perTitleFindings.subject: an instrument that becomes the result: two BigInt traps in the new ring
perTitleFindings.evidence: Math.max on BigInt sections broke the machine at 0x46ea5c (a fault at the CRT bootstrap), and address>>>0 on the BigInt hook argument threw the same error, while the import hook beside it already reads Number(address)
perTitleFindings.port: the ring is opt-in under TH_TRACE_EIP, converts both the sections and the callback address explicitly, and attaches only to a fault

perTitleFindings.subject: the interior-call frame is derived from the image, and its first two rules were wrong
perTitleFindings.evidence: docs/porting/oracle-interior-calls.json holds 81 targets with 46 needing slots; the sum-of-pops rule said six slots for 0x44acd0 where the shared epilogue pops three, and the first-ret rule misses an epilogue reached through jnp
perTitleFindings.port: slots = the contiguous run of pops immediately before the LAST ret in the block, with the function end taken as its padding; each row keeps its balance and the call sites that named it, and the harness applies the map under TH_INTERIOR_CALLS

perTitleFindings.subject: an instrument can be applied and ineffective: the frame went above the return address
perTitleFindings.evidence: map on with the slots pushed first gave pc=0x0 at esp=stackBase=0x7efff00 while map off gave esp=0x7efff0c, twelve bytes above the base; the epilogue pops upward, so a slot above the return address is popped by ret instead of the address
perTitleFindings.port: the slots are pushed after the return address is written, in pop order, and the measured effect is player-motion moving from UC_ERR_FETCH_UNMAPPED at pc 0x0 to UC_ERR_READ_UNMAPPED at address 0x78 with the return address 0x455b15 on the stack

perTitleFindings.subject: the four spawn-mode rows are unanchored, and shape cannot separate them
perTitleFindings.evidence: they are the same code with different literals - same two shared helpers, same shape, one private helper each (0x4556e0, 0x455760, 0x4557e0, 0x455860) - and the run matcher gave all four the same candidates headed by a five-instruction address
perTitleFindings.port: the rows stay withdrawn; the four helpers are the key, and a foothold in that family is what the next round needs

perTitleFindings.subject: four derivation routes measured as refusals, not assumed
perTitleFindings.evidence: masked-shape class search: 0 members in th12; --derive-calls over 147 anchored bases: 0 derived, every caller unanchored; call sequence: blocked because 0x456910 is unsettled; settled globals: one shared reference (0x4c3810 -> 0x4cee78) used by 622 th12 entries
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-shape-classes.py is kept as the class-search instrument, and the remaining instrument is behavioural comparison under the oracle

perTitleFindings.subject: the class-search instrument had four defects, each one producing the same zero
perTitleFindings.evidence: per-side wildcards (masked positions recomputed on the target), raw instead of mapped ranges (0 of 96 bytes wildcarded on a window whose first instruction reads a global), candidate set limited to call targets and padding, and an operand rule that missed register-relative displacements
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-shape-classes.py now takes the wildcards from the source window, uses mapped ranges, scans the whole section under the alignment rule, and masks the disp32 of a MEM operand with a base or index register

perTitleFindings.subject: the family granularity is the class, and field offsets move between titles
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x455760 and 0x455860 are byte-identical in th11 once operands are masked and both match 0x4612d0 by shape with a hit count of two; the shape-equal pair differs in exactly six instructions, all of them moved operands such as [edx+0x7b562c] against [edx+0x8856b8]
perTitleFindings.port: match this family class to class by instruction shape, not byte to byte; keep the byte-level class search for the functions whose operands do not move

perTitleFindings.subject: the class-search instrument was answering a stronger question than the method asks
perTitleFindings.evidence: the anchored row for 0x401fd0 records span 48, literals 48, run 16, i.e. a longest agreeing literal run; the tool demanded full-window byte equality, which no row in the table meets, so every target class was 0 including known-correct rows
perTitleFindings.port: the class search now uses the method own criterion, is validated by reproducing the 0x401fd0 row exactly and alone, and four further defects were fixed on the way (per-side wildcards, raw ranges, an entry-list candidate universe, and over-masking of small displacements)

perTitleFindings.subject: the helper family has a class-level anchor: {0x455760, 0x455860} to {0x4612d0, 0x4613d0}
perTitleFindings.evidence: both helpers give two boundary hits with agreement 48/48 and are one class on the source side as well; 0x4556e0 and 0x4557e0 have run 8 and no twin, and the four spawn functions run 14 and no twin
perTitleFindings.port: use the settled helper class as the foothold section 97.4 needed, and keep the spawn rows withdrawn until a class-level match exists for them

perTitleFindings.subject: a table candidate was the weaker of two, and the span decided it
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x4540f0 had candidate 0x44f442 in the table; both it and 0x45fbf0 agree on every literal byte at 48 bytes, only 0x45fbf0 agrees at 96 and 128, and neither agrees at 256
perTitleFindings.port: the row is now 0x4540f0 -> 0x0045fbf0 with confidence measured and its evidence recorded; the span is the tiebreaker when the method criterion admits more than one candidate

perTitleFindings.subject: the settlement turned a suite green: anm-resource flips to passing, 22 passing, none regressed
perTitleFindings.evidence: the suite previously failed at unmapped@0x0 pc=0x45fbff, which is inside the settled target region and inside the other copy of the routine; touch miss 0x4540f0 is gone from the logs
perTitleFindings.port: the same span-decided settlement can be applied to the two remaining candidate rows and to the withdrawn spawn rows once their class has a member that survives a longer window

perTitleFindings.subject: the interior-call map derives the epilogue but not the prologue frame setup
perTitleFindings.evidence: a suite entering 0x45fbf0 directly runs with ebp = 0 and its first frame store is mov dword ptr [ebp+0x38], 3 at 0x432cc1, an unmapped write at 0x38
perTitleFindings.port: derive the prologue frame setup (the register the prologue loads as the frame pointer) for the same interior entries, by the rule already used for the epilogue pops

perTitleFindings.subject: the prologue frame is derived per entry, and it moved four suites with no regression
perTitleFindings.evidence: 24 of 87 interior entries use [ebp+disp] while the prologue before the label does not set EBP; applying a scratch frame only for those moves player-frame, player-options, player-rendering and shot-resource off the null-frame store class to a fetch at zero, with the census at 22 passing, nothing flipped and nothing regressed
perTitleFindings.port: machine.mjs sets EBP to 0x07f10000 for those entries under TH_INTERIOR_FRAME=0; the blanket default round 307 refuted stays refuted, and the rule fires on a derived subset

perTitleFindings.subject: call_targets padding entries had kept the case at hand out of the interior map
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x432cc0, the label the player-frame suite calls, was in the call-target index as a padding entry, so the map skipped it; filtering to entries a direct E8 reaches raised the map from 81 to 87 targets and produced the row with usesEbp true and setsEbp false
perTitleFindings.port: the padding filter alone moves no wall, which was measured by rerunning the four suites with the frame rule off and the new map in place

perTitleFindings.subject: a pc = 0x0 fault is now a reading: where the return address was planted, whether it is held, and the drift
perTitleFindings.evidence: player-frame framePlan returnSlot 0x7effefc, slots 0, esp 0x7effefc; fault esp 0x7efff84 returnDrift 34 returnHeld false returnValue 0x0, plus the word the ret pops = 35 words = 0x8c
perTitleFindings.port: machine.mjs attaches framePlan, returnDrift, returnHeld and returnValue to the fault

perTitleFindings.subject: the frame that 0x432cc0 skips is a /GS frame, and the epilogue release is 0x6c
perTitleFindings.evidence: sub esp,0x6c at 0x4329a0, the cookie at [0x4ad138], EBP loaded from [esp+0x74] as the first argument, and the epilogue mov ecx,[esp+0x70]; pop edi; pop ebp; xor ecx,esp; call __security_check_cookie; add esp,0x6c; ret 4
perTitleFindings.port: the pop run is not contiguous with the ret, which is why the contiguous-run slot rule reported 0

perTitleFindings.subject: the reservation amount is probed to the byte: 108 + 28, and 136 clears the class
perTitleFindings.evidence: drift 34 with no reservation, 7 at 108 bytes, 4 at 120 and zero at 136, where the unmapped fault disappears; the prefix-sum 176 instead regresses the census to 17 passing
perTitleFindings.port: the reservation is derived and carried but off by default, with TH_INTERIOR_STACK_BYTES to probe

perTitleFindings.subject: three static derivations of the interior stack requirement, all refuted by the probed amount
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x432cc0 needs 136 bytes by probe (drift 7 at 108, 4 at 120, 0 at 136); the prefix sum says 176, the balance at the label 124 and the forward walk to the first ret 56, and the three disagree with each other as well as with the probe
perTitleFindings.port: the requirement is an executed-path property; the map keeps all three quantities with their provenance and the reservation stays off

perTitleFindings.subject: the next instrument is execution, with the census as the acceptance test
perTitleFindings.evidence: the machine records the executed pc sequence for a fault and the frame plan records the planted return slot and the drift from it, so the requirement can be measured by running once at zero and applying exactly the measured drift
perTitleFindings.port: a self-calibrating interior frame requiring returnHeld true and drift zero, judged by the census

perTitleFindings.subject: the interior call now ends on the planted return address: the return-site repair, slot and ESP
perTitleFindings.evidence: the ring shows the path reaching 0x4336c9 after call __security_check_cookie while the planted slot holds 0x4336c6; restoring the slot and ESP makes 0x432cc0 return, with the next fault at an unrelated entry 0x431070 and returnDrift 0
perTitleFindings.port: machine.mjs hooks every ret of the function for the call and restores the slot and ESP only when either is wrong, under TH_INTERIOR_RET=0

perTitleFindings.subject: an empty catch swallowed a ReferenceError and made a working repair look like a no-op
perTitleFindings.evidence: on and off player-frame failed identically with returnDrift 34 until u.HOOK_CODE inside call() was changed to this.uc.HOOK_CODE; u is a const local to init()
perTitleFindings.port: a failed hook install is recorded in recent as ret-hook-failed rather than eaten

perTitleFindings.subject: four per-call resets were inside a comment, so fault, recent and calls were never reset
perTitleFindings.evidence: this.fault=null; this.recent.length=0; the eipRing reset and ++this.calls sat on the tail of a prose comment; every payload in the previous four rounds reported calls: 0
perTitleFindings.port: the statements have their own line; pass/fail is unchanged, which is what a diagnostics-only defect should look like

perTitleFindings.subject: the return-site repair does not yet make the section 96 slots redundant
perTitleFindings.evidence: TH_INTERIOR_SLOTS=0 leaves the census at 22 passing with nothing flipped and nothing regressed, but moves twelve walls, none of them a pass, and turns five guest-level import readings into host-level RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds
perTitleFindings.port: the slots stay on by default and the switch is kept so the question can be re-asked

perTitleFindings.subject: the epilogue is not a contiguous run of pops: 45 of 87 interior rows had too few slots
perTitleFindings.evidence: the /GS epilogue separates its pops from the ret with the cookie check and the frame release, so the contiguous-run rule reported zero for 0x432cc0 and the epilogue popped the machine planted return address; enemy-frame showed EDI holding 0x7f00000
perTitleFindings.port: epilogue_pops walks back from the last ret, skipping the release and the cookie check and stopping at a push, another ret or a branch; the old count stays in the map as contiguous

perTitleFindings.subject: the sentinel leak is now a metric, and it is a floor rather than a measure of correctness
perTitleFindings.evidence: scanSentinel reports registers holding 0x7f00000; player-frame 5 (EDI, ESI, EBP), player-rendering 1, enemy-frame 0; raising the slots from 4 to 8 LOWERED the count from 5 to 3 while the popped values stayed wrong
perTitleFindings.port: TH_SENTINEL_REPORT prints the per-process leak line; read it next to the census

perTitleFindings.subject: the section 105 walk crossed a return path and gave 0x432cc0 each register twice
perTitleFindings.evidence: saves were esi ebx edi ebp esi ebx edi ebp until the walk stopped at the second ret; five rows still carry a duplicate pair and are recorded rather than hidden
perTitleFindings.port: epilogue_pops stops at the second ret; over-counting is not safe either, because extra slots move ESP down and shift the entered code [esp+disp] reads

perTitleFindings.subject: the sentinel leak is attributed to its call, and its origin is 0x44acd0 leaving EDI
perTitleFindings.evidence: samples read 0x44acd0->0x7f00000 EDI in player-frame, player-motion and player-rendering; the row is slots=3 for the last ret but the function holds six returns, so the executed path decides which pops happen
perTitleFindings.port: scanSentinel records this.currentCall with each leak

perTitleFindings.subject: the machine now refuses to push the sentinel as a slot value
perTitleFindings.evidence: player-frame went from 5 leaks to 3 with scrubbed 1; the ESI entry that came from propagation disappeared while the attributed origin stayed
perTitleFindings.port: slotValue substitutes zero and counts the substitution as scrubbed N

perTitleFindings.subject: the return-site repair now restores registers, and the sentinel leak reaches zero
perTitleFindings.evidence: a register holding the sentinel at a hooked ret is restored to the value the call supplied for it, the caller own value; player-frame 3->0, player-rendering 1->0, player-motion 2->0, with scrubbed 0, so no substitute was needed
perTitleFindings.port: the ret hook restores ESP, the planted slot and any register still holding the sentinel

perTitleFindings.subject: the corpus-wide sentinel figure is zero, and the report had been discarded rather than absent
perTitleFindings.evidence: 142 suites, 107 processes reporting, 0 registers holding 0x7f00000 and 0 scrubbed; the census runner captured the suites stdout and parsed only pass/fail, so TH_SENTINEL_REPORT looked like it did nothing
perTitleFindings.port: census-306.mjs --leaks sets the environment itself and aggregates the line

perTitleFindings.subject: the census verdict table is committed, and a filtered run cannot overwrite it
perTitleFindings.evidence: a --filter game-resources run replaced the whole corpus table in tools/tmp with a one-row file, silently; the file parsed and was wrong
perTitleFindings.port: full runs write docs/porting/census-th12.json, filtered runs census-th12-filtered.json, --out names a file

perTitleFindings.subject: two thirds of the walls are one class, and the class is the executed path again
perTitleFindings.evidence: null-base 47, garbage-base 14, import-stub 6 read out of the committed verdict; the shared site 0x454ee1 read directly gives a null base plus 0x11c with slots 0, args 5 and a ten word return drift
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-wall-classes.py groups the committed table by address class

perTitleFindings.subject: the verdict table entry and calls columns read None because their field path is stale
perTitleFindings.evidence: the runner reads trap.target.entry and the trap payloads no longer nest it there, so two columns have been empty since the payload shape changed
perTitleFindings.port: recorded rather than worked around; the columns are to be repaired or removed

perTitleFindings.subject: the verdict entry and calls columns now read the payload the wrapper prints
perTitleFindings.evidence: trap.target is the title metadata, trap is an empty object and recent entries carry only at/type/address/size/pc, so the two columns had no source; parsing the captured output gives entry 0x40a250 calls 18 for bullet-manager, the same values section 111.2 read by hand
perTitleFindings.port: both columns are parsed from the captured payload and are null rather than zero when a suite reaches no call

perTitleFindings.subject: the interior map has no gap; a 27-entry gap was a key-normalization error of my own
perTitleFindings.evidence: a scratch script normalized map keys with replace("0x00","0x"), turning 0x00401670 into 0x401670 (seven digits) so it never matched the verdict; the tool-native audit reports 89 suite-called addresses, 87 covered, 2 real entries and 0 missing rows
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-interior-calls.py --audit answers the coverage question against the row set the tool itself writes

perTitleFindings.subject: a write whose argument can raise truncated the plan; build the bytes first
perTitleFindings.evidence: io.open(PLAN,'wb') ran before the TypeError from SECTION.rstrip(b'\n'), so the plan was emptied and the write never happened; plan printed 0 bytes and 0 sections; restored byte-identical from HEAD
perTitleFindings.port: records build their bytes into a variable first and write once, then print the size as evidence

perTitleFindings.subject: verifiedAtHead is the browser probe snapshot, not a commit hash
perTitleFindings.evidence: the field holds error, framesThisRun, pageErrors, phase, stage and th12; a stale-commit claim about it was dropped
perTitleFindings.port: read it as the verification snapshot it is; the head is in the commit history

perTitleFindings.subject: the null-base shortlist names a short row as the next target
perTitleFindings.evidence: 36 null-base sites over 47 suites; five of the largest name entries absent from the map, which section 113 showed are real entries; the only large site with an empty row is 0x415518 via entry 0x004154d0 with slots=0 and reserve=32
perTitleFindings.port: tools/th-null-base-targets.py joins the committed verdict to the map by integer address and quotes each row rather than recalling it

perTitleFindings.subject: the short-row site reads a null register and the row reserve of 32 is not applied
perTitleFindings.evidence: identical payloads in enemy-emitter-commands and enemy-state-commands: [reg+4] with EDX, ESI and EDI zero, args 0, slots 0, reserve 32 unapplied because reservation is off by default
perTitleFindings.port: measure a selective reserve where reserve>0 and slots==0 against the census

perTitleFindings.subject: returnDrift at an interior site must be read with the call depth it was taken at
perTitleFindings.evidence: returnDrift -202 at pc 0x415518 is guest nesting, not a mis-supplied frame, because the guest own calls push their own frames
perTitleFindings.port: do not read a large negative drift as damage at an interior site

perTitleFindings.subject: the selective reserve reached the site, changed it by 32 bytes, and did not move the wall
perTitleFindings.evidence: framePlan.esp 0x7effefc -> 0x7effedc = -32 and returnDrift -202 -> -210, while pc 0x415518 keeps the same [reg+4] read with EDX, ESI and EDI zero
perTitleFindings.port: the unapplied reserve is refuted as the cause of the null base at this site

perTitleFindings.subject: the selective reserve regresses the census and is reverted, with the run committed
perTitleFindings.evidence: passing 22 -> 17, trapping 67 -> 73, leaks 0 -> 2 over 106 reporting processes, eight walls moved including anm-resource and archive which had no wall at all
perTitleFindings.port: docs/porting/census-th12-reserve-selector.json holds the refuted run; machine.mjs is byte-identical to HEAD

perTitleFindings.subject: 0x4154d0 is a function start in the image, not an interior label
perTitleFindings.evidence: SEH frame, /GS cookie, push ebp / mov ebp esp / and esp -8, sub esp 0x308, push ebx esi edi; the wall is mov eax,[esi+4] with ESI zero
perTitleFindings.port: an entry reached only indirectly has a row in the map whose facts come from the wrong enclosing entry

perTitleFindings.subject: covered is not correct: section 113 audit is not a completeness claim
perTitleFindings.evidence: the tool real-entry rule is a direct E8 target, which cannot see an entry reached through a pointer or table, so 0x004154d0 was given an interior row
perTitleFindings.port: read the image at a row address before trusting the row

perTitleFindings.subject: the wall is a register argument the machine cannot supply
perTitleFindings.evidence: call() accepts ecx, edx and stack args only; both suites call touch(0x412e30) and never 0x4154d0, so ESI was zero at the entry
perTitleFindings.port: find the indirect call site and read what it loads into ESI before adding an optional register supply

perTitleFindings.subject: 0x004154d0 has no reference anywhere in the shipped image
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0 dwords, 0 immediates in .text, 0 relative jmps to it or to its thunk 0x004154c0; agrees with round 150 runtime finding of zero direct callers
perTitleFindings.port: the call target came from the harness checkpoint tables, not from the game code

perTitleFindings.subject: the payload entry is the machine call target, not title metadata
perTitleFindings.evidence: machine.mjs line 246 sets this.fault.entry=hex(address) inside call()
perTitleFindings.port: a call with target 0x004154d0 really happened

perTitleFindings.subject: ESI, EDI and EBX are optional register arguments and are provably inert
perTitleFindings.evidence: identical payloads in both suites and a full census at 22 passing / 67 trapping / 0 leaks with 0 flipped, 0 regressed and 0 walls moved
perTitleFindings.port: liveness of the supply is not yet shown; pass the enemy pointer in esi on the 0x4154d0 path next

perTitleFindings.subject: the instruction ring was being discarded on every trap
perTitleFindings.evidence: it is reset per call and the trap artifact carried recent, trap and errorFields but not the fault; errorFields is empty because it serialises primitives of the error object
perTitleFindings.port: helpers.mjs writes fault and eipRing; the switch is TH_TRACE_EIP, not TH_EIP_RING

perTitleFindings.subject: the call to 0x4154d0 came from the harness, not from the game path
perTitleFindings.evidence: the ring is reset per call, so its first entry 0x4154d0 is the address the machine was called at; a jump from the thunk would have started the ring in the enclosing function
perTitleFindings.port: supply the enemy pointer in esi at that harness call and read the wall again

perTitleFindings.subject: the caller of 0x4154d0 is the test, via touch() translating a th11 address
perTitleFindings.evidence: TH_CALL_TRACE shows the seventh call at 0x4154d0 from TestContext.<anonymous>; touch() maps the th11 dispatcher address to th12 0x4154d0, so no constant exists in the image
perTitleFindings.port: the ring names the target, not the caller; use the JavaScript stack for caller questions

perTitleFindings.subject: ESI is derived from ECX at +0x174c, it is not an argument
perTitleFindings.evidence: mov ebx,ecx; mov esi,[ebx+0x174c]; mov eax,[esi+4]; writing manager at n+0x174c and calling with ecx=n moves the wall from address 0x4 to address 0x7de64de0
perTitleFindings.port: section 118/119 reading is corrected; the optional esi/edi/ebx arguments are inert but not the fix

perTitleFindings.subject: touch() translates addresses but not structure offsets
perTitleFindings.evidence: the th11 fixture passes q = n+0x103c and th12 reads [ecx+0x174c], a th11 layout against th12 code
perTitleFindings.port: audit how many suites pass a translated address where the callee indexes a field

perTitleFindings.subject: 14 of 81 translated call targets derive a pointer from a supplied register
perTitleFindings.evidence: tools/th-derived-args.py over 178 translation rows and 139 call sites; flags include 0x4154d0 [ebx+0x174c] and screen-shake reading [edi+0x1c] while only ECX is passed
perTitleFindings.port: work the queue: check whether each site supplies the register the body dereferences

perTitleFindings.subject: the audit itself produced a plausible negative until it was tested on a known case
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0 of 81 from an RVA-vs-VA bug that disassembled nothing, a 10-instruction window shorter than the 20th instruction where mov ebx,ecx sits, and a crash on absolute addressing
perTitleFindings.port: test an audit on a known positive before believing its counts

perTitleFindings.subject: the never-supplied bucket was empty by construction and its six entries were artifacts
perTitleFindings.evidence: derives() only follows aliases seeded from supplied registers, so a copy-derived base is supplied by definition; the bucket compared the copy EBX against the origin ECX at 0x4154d0
perTitleFindings.port: the report now carries base, origin and displacement per target instead of a manufactured defect

perTitleFindings.subject: fourteen targets carry a displacement the suite object must satisfy
perTitleFindings.evidence: disp values include +0x174c (measured in 121.3), +0x478 on three targets, +0x100c, +0xc
perTitleFindings.port: measure each site by passing the base register and reading whether the wall moves

perTitleFindings.subject: 16 of the 17 flagged suites are failing; the 17th is the correct-site control
perTitleFindings.evidence: crossing the derived-argument audit with the committed verdict; menu-cursor passes and its body reads [edx+8] from the register it is given
perTitleFindings.port: the flags are candidates, not causes: enemy-phase:10 already writes the flagged field

perTitleFindings.subject: the priority tool printed a false all-clear because it read the wrong field name
perTitleFindings.evidence: the verdict rows carry pass and fail; the tool looked for passed/status/result and printed "flagged AND failing: 0"
perTitleFindings.port: when a report says 0 problems, test the extractor against a known-problem case

perTitleFindings.subject: two heaps: c.allocate and m.allocate, and touch() translates addresses not pointer values
perTitleFindings.evidence: bullet-manager allocates data=c.allocate(source.length) and manager=m.allocate(0x46d680) in one line; supplying manager+4 does not move the wall at 0x004154d0

perTitleFindings.subject: section 121.3 was wrong: the planted field was overwritten before the call

perTitleFindings.subject: the dispatcher chain, fed link by link with attribution

perTitleFindings.subject: the suites that reach 0x4154d0 trap because they build that field from random data

perTitleFindings.subject: the +0x174c field is a member used repeatedly by the dispatcher caller
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x00415c53 and 0x00415c74 both load [ebx+0x174c] then [eax+4] and pass it to 0x468ec0

perTitleFindings.subject: the suites need an object-relocation bridge, not hand-written offsets

perTitleFindings.subject: the dispatcher context shape is a mask plus an argument array
perTitleFindings.evidence: FUN_00468e20 and FUN_00468ec0 read [ctx+4] -> instruction, word mask at +8, arguments at +0x10+index*4, and [ctx+0x100c]

perTitleFindings.subject: wiring the chain moves the census wall for the first time in the session

perTitleFindings.subject: the bridge is a keeper and the wall movement is now committed

perTitleFindings.subject: a flagged suite needs three things, not one

perTitleFindings.subject: the trapping count drops for the first time, 67 to 66

perTitleFindings.subject: the mirror audit produced a false negative on the one fixed suite, and its mirror column is unreliable
perTitleFindings.evidence: the offset moved into the helper module so a literal scan cannot see it; emitter builds its mirror field by field and is reported as having none

perTitleFindings.subject: the import-stub wall 0x7e00ce0 was a symptom of the missing object graph
perTitleFindings.evidence: one of the six import-stub sites disappears entirely when enemy-animations is bridged: 0x7e00ce0 -> None

perTitleFindings.subject: two bridged suites do not move because they fail before the dispatcher
perTitleFindings.evidence: cancellation-integration and laser-manager keep the same pc; their queue flag came from using touch(0x412e30) while their wall is elsewhere

perTitleFindings.subject: the displacement queue is a list of candidates, not of causes
perTitleFindings.evidence: all ten dispatcher suites are bridged, four of them move nothing because they trap elsewhere (bullet-manager 0x454ee1, rectangle-cancellation 0x40b3a3)

perTitleFindings.subject: the fidelity targets are port-side and belong to the cpp lane

perTitleFindings.subject: more than half of the failing suites are assertion failures, not crashes
perTitleFindings.evidence: verdict rows: 120 failing, 65 trapping, 56 non-trapping

perTitleFindings.subject: the largest null-base class is a function entry expecting an object
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x00454ee0 push edi; 0x00454ee1 mov edi,[ecx+0x11c]; four suites reach it with ecx=0

perTitleFindings.subject: a stale trap artifact can attribute a wall to a passing suite
perTitleFindings.evidence: th12-aim-angle.test.mjs pass=1 fail=0 carried wall pc=0x419629 from newestTrap(); rows now carry code and wallCounted

perTitleFindings.subject: row fail counts assertions, so three different "failed suites" totals are defensible
perTitleFindings.evidence: fail>0 = 114, not pass = 120, plus one passing row with a wall = 121; 6 rows died before any test

perTitleFindings.subject: a suite that pins the original fault behaviour is a fidelity result, not a wall
perTitleFindings.evidence: th12-aim-angle asserts the original faults with a non-reference argument and passes; its artifact is expected
perTitleFindings.port: wall classes separate pinned-fault rows so the next target is not chosen from an inflated class

perTitleFindings.subject: the four-suite null-base class has eight entry points
perTitleFindings.evidence: tools/th-callers.py, self-tested against two hand-found callers, lists 8 for 0x454ee0
perTitleFindings.port: trace the chain from the caller the suite actually reaches, not the first one read

perTitleFindings.subject: the corpus largest trap site is two unmodelled pointers
perTitleFindings.evidence: [global 0x4b44f4] -> manager, [manager+0x488] past the end of a 0x480 allocation, and [object+0x11c]; supplying both ends the trap and the census drops to 63

perTitleFindings.subject: the port differs from the original on the initialize 0/0 0x3c field
perTitleFindings.evidence: laser-line: actual=0x41820000 expected=0xffffffff
perTitleFindings.port: port-side; reported here rather than edited, because cpp/game belongs to another lane

perTitleFindings.subject: the two-field class answer generalises to the sibling suite

perTitleFindings.subject: the bullet path reaches the same function through a stack-supplied base
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x40a809 mov ecx,[esp+0x24]; 0x40a821 mov ecx,[ecx+0x4debdc]; 0x40a835 call 0x454ee0
perTitleFindings.port: measure that base rather than transplanting the laser global

perTitleFindings.subject: the bullet path argument is null because its base object is too small
perTitleFindings.evidence: a hook at 0x454ee0 shows ecx=0; the base manager is 0x46d680 bytes and the slot read is at +0x4debdc; growing it to 0x4e0000 ends the trap
