perTitleFindings.subject: an inference refused by the machine is a measurement, not an obstacle
perTitleFindings.evidence: the artifact stack reading implied 0x83debdc, and the machine answered Guest memory bounds 0x83debdc + 4, which is why the register was hooked instead
perTitleFindings.port: prefer a hook that prints the register over a reading of the artifact layout

perTitleFindings.subject: the corpus largest trap site is empty
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x454ee1 held four suites at section 132 and holds none; trapping 61 -> 60 with 0 flipped and 0 regressed
perTitleFindings.port: the next target comes from the remaining three-suite sites, each a fresh chain

perTitleFindings.subject: the r358 report figure of 44 disagrees with its own committed verdict of 43
perTitleFindings.port: the sixth member of the reporting family; caught by diffing committed verdicts, not by re-reading

perTitleFindings.subject: the 0x4067e0 wall is a null edi, a parameter nobody set
perTitleFindings.evidence: the fault on [eax+0x10] at 0x78 with eax=0x68 comes from 0x455b0d lea eax,[edi+0x68]; edi is used ten times and loaded never in the body
perTitleFindings.port: find the address the game enters that body at before changing the suite

perTitleFindings.subject: a tool sentence that names its own input is not a finding
perTitleFindings.evidence: the window tool says 0x4559d0 is a boundary in the sweep from entry 0x4559d0, and its picture there is misaligned decoding
perTitleFindings.port: refute a boundary claim whose only support is the tool starting there, before writing it down

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm wall is a null argument, not a missing field
perTitleFindings.evidence: the body is entered at 0x455630 with mov edi,[ebp+8], so edi is its first stack argument, and the three suites never call that range or set EDI
perTitleFindings.port: the fix is on the calling path; follow the suite call that reaches 0x455630

perTitleFindings.subject: listing call targets settles an entry question that a tool sentence could not
perTitleFindings.evidence: only two addresses in [0x455000,0x455a00) are called, so the entry is 0x455630
perTitleFindings.port: ask who is called rather than asking whether an address looks like a boundary

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm wall arrives as a null first argument, not created in the path
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x454d10 mov esi,[ebp+8] then four push esi / call 0x455630 sites; 0x455630 does mov edi,[ebp+8]
perTitleFindings.port: supply arg1 on the calling path; the body itself matches the 0x454ee1/0x454ee7 pattern

perTitleFindings.subject: int3 padding names a function entry when no call does
perTitleFindings.evidence: int3 at 0x454d0f precedes 0x454d10, whose prologue is push ebp / mov ebp,esp
perTitleFindings.port: use it where a body is entered indirectly and no direct call target exists

perTitleFindings.subject: the two anm suites share a call site but not a path
perTitleFindings.evidence: hooking 0x454d10 in shot-manager never fires, yet its wall frame returns to 0x455b15, the same site anm-scripts uses
perTitleFindings.port: find the indirect entry the suites use; direct call listings cannot see it

perTitleFindings.subject: a replaced function returns to 0x7f00000
perTitleFindings.evidence: the hook run prints ret=0x7f00000 for an ordinary call, which explains the stack word section 137 misread
perTitleFindings.port: do not read a hook return address as a game address

perTitleFindings.subject: setting one register moved a wall the callee appeared not to use
perTitleFindings.evidence: the callee first instruction reads [eax+0x10] yet shot-manager needed m.reg(EDI,np) before the call; the wall moved from 0x4067e0 to 0x45568c
perTitleFindings.port: set every register a directly called entry can reach, not just the arguments

perTitleFindings.subject: shot-manager calls the wall function directly
perTitleFindings.evidence: touch(0x406100) prints 0x4067e0
perTitleFindings.port: the 0x455630 chain belongs to anm-scripts; each suite needs its own mapping measured

perTitleFindings.subject: 0x455a00 is an address inside the function at 0x455630
perTitleFindings.evidence: no int3 boundary between 0x455630 and 0x455a00; the prologue at 0x455630 is the only one
perTitleFindings.port: entering mid-function leaves ebp stale, so [ebp+8] holds whatever the machine left

perTitleFindings.subject: a single 0xCC inside code is not padding
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x454dc0, 0x454def and six more single int3 bytes sit between ordinary instructions
perTitleFindings.port: require a run of at least two int3 and a prologue-shaped first instruction

perTitleFindings.subject: the artifact entry is the JS call target, not a frame
perTitleFindings.evidence: machine.mjs line 266 assigns this.fault.entry=hex(address) in the trap builder
perTitleFindings.port: trace the fixture call that passes the address; a suite line may not be the one

perTitleFindings.subject: a stack value is not a live frame
perTitleFindings.evidence: shot-damage shows 0x455b15 in its stack window while hooks on 0x455630 and 0x454d10 never print
perTitleFindings.port: hook the address before asserting the path runs through it

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm spawn fixture enters a th12 function from the middle
perTitleFindings.evidence: anm-oracle.mjs line 46 calls touch(0x455a00); section 144 shows no boundary between 0x455630 and 0x455a00
perTitleFindings.port: fix the mapping in fixture-addresses.mjs and the convention in anm-oracle.mjs together

perTitleFindings.subject: retargeting the entry alone moves a wall and breaks two handle contracts
perTitleFindings.evidence: with 0x455630, anm-scripts reaches 0x45568c while shot-damage and shot-manager fail actual 0 expected 1
perTitleFindings.port: the th12 entry signature differs, so the fixture must adapt as well

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm spawn assertion is a fidelity comparison, not a fixture contract
perTitleFindings.evidence: shot-manager.test.mjs:34 asserts o.spawn(...) equals the core anm_manager_spawn handle
perTitleFindings.port: a zero from the oracle is a fidelity miss to report against the port

perTitleFindings.subject: two candidate th12 spawn entries are excluded by measurement
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x455a00 traps at 0x4067e0; 0x455630 with correct args yields slot=0, EAX=0, return=0
perTitleFindings.port: find the entry from the core pointer the suite already reads

perTitleFindings.subject: the oracle anm spawn must return the vm id counter, not a pointer
perTitleFindings.evidence: the suite reads the u32 at the returned pointer and the core sets that field from next_id
perTitleFindings.port: a candidate entry that returns 0 or an address is wrong even if it accepts the arguments

perTitleFindings.subject: the th12 spawn entry runs one ANM update before returning
perTitleFindings.evidence: AnmManager::create calls vm->update before assigning the id and returns nullptr if it fails
perTitleFindings.port: the oracle entry must be the outer function, not the allocator or a post-update body

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm stack does not read the manager global 0x4b4514
perTitleFindings.evidence: 116 references to the global, none in 0x450000-0x460000 where the anm code lives
perTitleFindings.port: the fixture manager may not be the object this code wants; verify before setting registers from it

perTitleFindings.subject: port and fixture manager layouts differ in size
perTitleFindings.evidence: core manager is 0x7bd900 bytes, fixture np is 0x8d40, and next_id is a member not a global
perTitleFindings.port: report only; address-level correspondence needs its own evidence

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm oracle manager and the suite manager are different objects
perTitleFindings.evidence: at the entry edi=0x2950c10 (the suite np) while the fixture manager 0x20031a0 appears nowhere
perTitleFindings.port: pass the manager the call is about explicitly; do not rely on a leftover register

perTitleFindings.subject: the spawn entry has correct inputs yet returns zero
perTitleFindings.evidence: args, ESI handle slot and EDI manager all correct; slot=0, EAX=0, return=0
perTitleFindings.port: the unproven part is now the id counter, not the inputs

perTitleFindings.subject: the retargeted anm spawn entry declines to run
perTitleFindings.evidence: a 0x1000-byte snapshot of the manager shows zero changed words across the call
perTitleFindings.port: zeros here mean a precondition failure, not a wrong id; do not read them as a miscount

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm-spawn chain is being widened, not deepened
perTitleFindings.evidence: five rounds produced measurements but no verdict movement, while 15 suites sit behind the garbage-base class
perTitleFindings.port: apply the proven instrument to the other classes

perTitleFindings.subject: the fault pc in the census is real evidence of execution
perTitleFindings.evidence: the row shows at:'unmapped' with address 0x41c31edc and pc 0x45568c, Unicorn's fault record
perTitleFindings.port: a silent probe at that pc means the probe was not installed in that test, not that the code did not run

perTitleFindings.subject: each test creates its own oracle machine
perTitleFindings.evidence: anm-geometry has three tests, each with const c=await core(),m=await oracle()
perTitleFindings.port: install probes per test or in a shared helper

perTitleFindings.subject: q+0x3f0 is a pointer in th12 and a float in the port
perTitleFindings.evidence: [edi+0x3f0] equals the fault address minus four, and the fixture randomises that offset as a float
perTitleFindings.port: layout divergence to report; the fixture must not randomise pointer fields

perTitleFindings.subject: the random vm drives the native interpreter to its instruction limit
perTitleFindings.evidence: with a readable buffer at q+0x3f0 the wall moves to 0x45a596 and Native instruction limit at 0x455697 appears
perTitleFindings.port: the field is the current ANM instruction pointer; the fixture needs a real script

perTitleFindings.subject: the quad test entry maps to a dispatcher, not to a geometry routine
perTitleFindings.evidence: 0x45cdf0 branches on [eax+0x47c] and calls 0x45a570, while the core anm_quad is pure geometry
perTitleFindings.port: a second suspect mapping: resolve it by matching the port function shape in the image

perTitleFindings.subject: the geometry wall is bracketed by two independent defects
perTitleFindings.evidence: q+0x3f0 is a pointer in th12 (section 153) and the entry is a dispatcher (section 154)
perTitleFindings.port: fixing either alone only relocates the trap

perTitleFindings.subject: the th12 geometry routine is 0x45a570 and the quad mapping is correct
perTitleFindings.evidence: it reproduces the port scale/extra_scale products and the parent dereference field for field
perTitleFindings.port: section 154 is corrected; the mapping needs no change

perTitleFindings.subject: the flags/mode word lives at 0x47c natively and 0x404 in the port, one bit apart
perTitleFindings.evidence: native shifts 0x13/0x17 against the port 18/22 at different offsets
perTitleFindings.port: fixtures must write the native word separately; report the offset/shift divergence

perTitleFindings.subject: the geometry routine is entered with the fixture vm but reads zero at 0x47c
perTitleFindings.evidence: ret=0x45ce1d, ecx=nativeOut, q==esi, and q+0x47c reads back 0 right after a write at two allocation sizes
perTitleFindings.port: verify the write path before touching the field layout

perTitleFindings.subject: a probe that skips an instruction can look like a fix
perTitleFindings.evidence: fail 3 -> fail 1 came from a hook on 0x45a5ac returning 0; the clean rebuild is fail 3 again
perTitleFindings.port: never credit an instrument that changes the system under test

perTitleFindings.subject: the oracle machine write path is sound, including +0x47c on an 0x800 allocation
perTitleFindings.evidence: four writes read back identically, including 0xcafebabe at +0x47c
perTitleFindings.port: the native vm needs an allocation that covers +0x47c; 0x434 does not

perTitleFindings.subject: two instruments were mathematically incapable of failing
perTitleFindings.evidence: a hook returning 0 skips its instruction; a zero-valued write test cannot detect a lost write
perTitleFindings.port: verify each instrument can fail before trusting its result

perTitleFindings.subject: the anm-geometry native output is a correct write of zeros
perTitleFindings.evidence: the routine stores [esi+0x430]+[esi+0x424]+[esi+0x43c], none of which the fixture randomises
perTitleFindings.port: the mismatch is two struct layouts fed one buffer, not a missing write

perTitleFindings.subject: the dispatcher mode-0 target is 0x45ce0b and the PE header offset is 0xc00
perTitleFindings.evidence: table read at 0x45ce4c with base 0x400c00, verified against the entry bytes
perTitleFindings.port: use base 0x400c00 for VA-to-file reads of this image

perTitleFindings.subject: the native geometry consumes 0x424/0x430/0x43c as a three-term Z sum
perTitleFindings.evidence: per-field sentinel sweep: exactly three offsets, each contributing 1.0 to all four vertices
perTitleFindings.port: the fixture must populate those offsets for the native side

perTitleFindings.subject: the fixture and the native vm disagree on where the Z terms live
perTitleFindings.evidence: the fixture randomises 0x3dc-0x3fc while the native reads 0x424/0x430/0x43c
perTitleFindings.port: sweep the core to tabulate its offsets, then build both layouts from one set of values

perTitleFindings.subject: the port position triple is 0x3dc-0x3fc and the native triple 0x41c-0x43c
perTitleFindings.evidence: both per-field sweeps, with the three Z terms mapping at a constant +0x40
perTitleFindings.port: a fixture can now feed both layouts the same physical position term by term

perTitleFindings.subject: the vertex component order differs between the layouts
perTitleFindings.evidence: the native Z term lands in the vertex leading word while the port order is {x,y,z}
perTitleFindings.port: mappings must carry values term by term, not memcpy a Vec3

perTitleFindings.subject: feeding both layouts from one set of values makes them compute the same quantity
perTitleFindings.evidence: the native writes -158.000 where the core writes -157.924, both the Z sum
perTitleFindings.port: the fixture plumbing is solved; the remaining differences are slot, numeric and function identity

perTitleFindings.subject: the native Z-only write pattern may mean a different helper is under test
perTitleFindings.evidence: only the vertices leading words are written natively while the port writes full vertices
perTitleFindings.port: check which function the mapping names before treating the mismatch as a port defect

perTitleFindings.subject: the port and native position triples correspond at a uniform +0x48
perTitleFindings.evidence: full-mask sweeps on both sides with identical w0/w1/w2 masks for all nine offsets
perTitleFindings.port: the native position triple begins at 0x424, the port at 0x3dc

perTitleFindings.subject: the two remaining geometry residuals are a scale factor and a branch difference
perTitleFindings.evidence: -485.0000 vs -483.0000, and a single native value across vertices where the port varies
perTitleFindings.port: identify the branch by varying anchors before treating either as a port defect

perTitleFindings.subject: the port quad geometry reproduces the original for controlled inputs
perTitleFindings.evidence: nine anchor combinations under mode 0 with known position produce identical vertices on both sides
perTitleFindings.port: positive fidelity result; the section 162 residuals are fixture artifacts

perTitleFindings.subject: agreement is only established for the controlled case
perTitleFindings.evidence: modes 1-3, scale, extra_scale, pivot, sprite size and rotation were all zero or unexercised
perTitleFindings.port: extend the matrix before claiming more

perTitleFindings.subject: the port horizontal scale pair is 0x3c+0x4c and the vertical pair 0x40+0x50
perTitleFindings.evidence: pairwise sweep with a known answer: the two pairs move x and y respectively
perTitleFindings.port: use these offsets when feeding the port the same extent as the native

perTitleFindings.subject: a product field is invisible to a single-field sweep
perTitleFindings.evidence: a clean null result over 0x2c..0x600 until the second factor was also set
perTitleFindings.port: use pairwise sweeps for any field that enters multiplicatively

perTitleFindings.subject: the port quad geometry is bit-identical for position plus scale plus all nine anchors
perTitleFindings.evidence: PROBE388C: nine of nine anchor combinations agree on raw 32-bit words, with outputs that vary by anchor
perTitleFindings.port: positive fidelity result with a sensitive instrument

perTitleFindings.subject: the native scale pairs are 0x40+0x58 and 0x44+0x5c
perTitleFindings.evidence: clean pairwise sweep over 0x2c..0x140 after excluding the position offsets
perTitleFindings.port: the native layout follows a regular +4/+0xc rearrangement for these factors

perTitleFindings.subject: the port extent machinery is exactly the two scale pairs
perTitleFindings.evidence: a sweep with a non-zero cofactor returns no further extent fields
perTitleFindings.port: no hidden sprite-size or pivot field remains

perTitleFindings.subject: modes 1-3 fault in the oracle under the current fixture
perTitleFindings.evidence: RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds for all nine anchor combinations
perTitleFindings.port: compare modes 1-3 only after the fixture carries the state those entries read

perTitleFindings.subject: the mode-1 path faults at pc 0x45b0ce dereferencing a zero pointer field
perTitleFindings.evidence: the fault record shows ECX=0 and EDI=0 with the mode-1 arithmetic constants still on the stack
perTitleFindings.port: supply the pointer field before comparing modes 1-3

perTitleFindings.subject: a fault record is readable even when the error carries no JSON suffix
perTitleFindings.evidence: reading m.fault directly after the trap returned pc, registers and stack
perTitleFindings.port: use m.fault rather than parsing the message

perTitleFindings.subject: the .text base is 0x401000, not the 0x400c00 section 158 derived
perTitleFindings.evidence: the PE section header plus the entry bytes 8b907c040000 at the header base
perTitleFindings.port: re-check every VA-to-file read made with 0x400c00

perTitleFindings.subject: the recorded mode-1 fault pc is a stack load, not a null dereference
perTitleFindings.evidence: fld dword ptr [esp+0x28] with esp=0x7effeb0, inside the guest stack

perTitleFindings.subject: the mode-1 trap is host-side (no type field) and value-independent
perTitleFindings.evidence: the fault record lacks type and an all-zero input still traps
perTitleFindings.port: no evidence against the port; modes 1-3 are unverified, not misverified

perTitleFindings.subject: the machine code bytes at the pc independently confirm the disassembly window
perTitleFindings.evidence: fault.code decodes to the same instructions as the image read with base 0x401000
perTitleFindings.port: the corrected base is safe for VA-to-file reads

perTitleFindings.subject: 0x400c00 is a file offset and 0x401000 is a VA base; both are correct
perTitleFindings.evidence: th12-case-body.py va2off = 0x400 + (va - 0x401000) = va - 0x400c00, and the helper returns 0x5c1f0 for 0x45cdf0
perTitleFindings.port: the repo tooling never used the wrong one; only an ad-hoc probe mixed them

perTitleFindings.subject: three independent sources decode 0x45b0ce identically
perTitleFindings.evidence: the repo instruction window, the hand-rolled window and the machine fault.code bytes
perTitleFindings.port: the corrected reading stands

perTitleFindings.subject: the quad geometry test now passes using the measured layout map
perTitleFindings.evidence: pass 1 fail 2 where it was pass 0 fail 3, with the quad test reporting 576 samples
perTitleFindings.port: the suite is now attributable: quad verified, ripple value mismatch, ring guest wall

perTitleFindings.subject: guest and host faults are distinguishable from the record shape alone
perTitleFindings.evidence: the ring fault carries type/address/recent; the mode-1 trap carries none of them
perTitleFindings.port: do not read memory access out of bounds as a guest diagnosis without checking type

perTitleFindings.subject: the native ring wall at 0x45568c was the fixture randomizing a float into a pointer field
perTitleFindings.evidence: [q+0x3f0] held the float 0x41c31ed8 before the call and 0x3f0 is in the randomized offset list
